```{python}
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Run from anywhere inside the repository.
ROOT = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents] if (p / "pyproject.toml").exists())
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

from tests.eval.passk import case_passes, pass_at_k, pass_at_k_bootstrap, pass_hat_k, pass_hat_k_bootstrap

JOBS = ROOT / ".harbor/jobs"
CASES = {c["id"]: c for c in map(json.loads, filter(str.strip, (ROOT / "eval_cases/cases.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()))}
MODES = {m["name"]: m for m in json.loads((ROOT / "analysis/state/patterns.json").read_text())["modes"]}
CI = json.loads((ROOT / "ci-runs.json").read_text())

# Cases shown in the video.
REGRESSION_EXAMPLE = "e-011"  # also the case broken on purpose in Part D
CAPABILITY_EXAMPLE = "e-004"
# Part E analyses: case -> 15-run Harbor job. e-004 uses code checks only;
# e-008 and e-009 are decided by the frozen narrates_or_overexplains-v6 judge.
TRIAL_COUNT_JOBS = {
    "e-004": "hw6-capability-15",
    "e-008": "hw6-capability-15-e-008",
    "e-009": "hw6-capability-15-e-009",
}
# e-009 and e-012 each had a VerifierTimeoutError in hw6-baseline, so their
# five baseline runs come from the rerun job.
BASELINE_JOB = {cid: "hw6-baseline-rerun" if cid in {"e-009", "e-012"} else "hw6-baseline" for cid in CASES}

INK, INK2, GRID, SURF = "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#e4e3df", "#fcfcfb"
SERIES = ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a"]  # categorical slots 1-3, same as HW5
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.facecolor": SURF, "axes.facecolor": SURF, "axes.edgecolor": GRID,
                     "axes.labelcolor": INK2, "xtick.color": INK2, "ytick.color": INK2,
                     "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False, "font.size": 10})

IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r"cw-[\w-]+|store-[\w-]+-policy|[Rr]efund (?:request )?ID:?\s*#?\d+")


def load_trial(d):
    """One Harbor trial: reward, check and judge components, judge critique, final reply."""
    result = json.loads((d / "result.json").read_text())
    reward = ((result.get("verifier_result") or {}).get("rewards") or {}).get("reward")
    comps = {}
    if (p := d / "verifier/reward-details.json").exists():
        comps = {c["name"]: c["detail"]["score"] for c in json.loads(p.read_text())["reward"]["components"]}
    critique = None
    if (p := d / "verifier/test-stdout.txt").exists():
        for line in p.read_text().splitlines():
            if line.startswith("JUDGE_RESULT "):
                critique = json.loads(line.removeprefix("JUDGE_RESULT "))["critique"]
    reply = None
    if (p := d / "agent/cartwheel-result.json").exists():
        turn = json.loads(p.read_text())["transcript"]["turns"][-1]
        reply = turn["messages"][-1] if turn.get("messages") else turn.get("reply")
    return {
        "name": d.name, "started": result["started_at"], "reward": reward,
        "error": bool(result.get("exception_info")), "checks": comps.get("checks"),
        "judge": next((v for k, v in comps.items() if k.startswith("judge_")), None),
        "critique": critique, "reply": reply,
    }


def trials(job, case_id):
    """Trials of one case in one job, in the order Harbor started them."""
    dirs = [d for d in (JOBS / job).glob(f"{case_id}__*") if d.is_dir()]
    return sorted((load_trial(d) for d in dirs), key=lambda t: t["started"])


def band(outcomes, ks, bootstrap):
    """95% bootstrap interval at each k, with the settings eval_results/ uses."""
    cis = [bootstrap(outcomes, k, samples=2000, seed=0) for k in ks]
    return [ci["ci95_low"] for ci in cis], [ci["ci95_high"] for ci in cis]


def table(headers, rows):
    lines = ["| " + " | ".join(headers) + " |", "|" + "---|" * len(headers)]
    lines += ["| " + " | ".join(str(x) for x in row) + " |" for row in rows]
    return Markdown("\n".join(lines))


def marks(rewards):
    return " ".join("✓" if r == 1 else "✗" for r in rewards)


def quote(text, highlight=False, literal=False):
    if literal:  # definitions use * as a wildcard (cw-*), not as emphasis
        text = text.replace("*", r"\*")
    if highlight:
        text = IDENTIFIER.sub(lambda m: f"**⟦{m.group(0)}⟧**", text)
    return "\n".join("> " + line for line in text.splitlines())


BASELINE = {cid: trials(BASELINE_JOB[cid], cid) for cid in CASES}
for cid, ts in BASELINE.items():
    assert len(ts) == 5 and not any(t["error"] or t["reward"] is None for t in ts), cid
```

## 2. Baseline runs and classification {#baseline}

Every case ran five times before it was classified. Five passes makes a case a **regression** case; any failure makes it a **capability** case, and the observed fraction becomes its `baseline_pass_rate`.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-baseline
#| tbl-cap: "Five baseline runs per case, in start order (✓ pass, ✗ fail)."
rows = []
for cid, ts in BASELINE.items():
    rewards = [t["reward"] for t in ts]
    c = sum(r == 1 for r in rewards)
    derived = "regression" if c == 5 else "capability"
    recorded = CASES[cid]["kind"]
    assert derived == recorded, cid
    rate = CASES[cid].get("baseline_pass_rate")
    rows.append((cid, f"`{CASES[cid]['mode']}`", marks(rewards), f"{c}/5", recorded,
                 "–" if rate is None else f"{rate:.1f}", BASELINE_JOB[cid]))
display(table(["Case", "Mode", "Runs", "Passes", "Kind", "Baseline rate", "Harbor job"], rows))
kinds = [c["kind"] for c in CASES.values()]
display(Markdown(f"Result: **{kinds.count('regression')} regression** and **{kinds.count('capability')} capability** cases. "
                 "The recorded `kind` matches the five runs for every case."))
```

```{python}
def show_case(cid, highlight=False):
    c, ts = CASES[cid], BASELINE[cid]
    display(Markdown(
        f"**{cid}** (`{c['mode']}`, {c['input']['role']}): {marks(t['reward'] for t in ts)}, "
        f"**{sum(t['reward'] == 1 for t in ts)}/5**, classified **{c['kind']}**.\n\n"
        f"User message:\n\n{quote(c['input']['message'])}\n\n"
        "Expected behavior:\n\n" + "\n".join(f"- {a}" for a in c["expected"]["assertions"])
    ))
    rows = [(i + 1, "✓" if t["reward"] == 1 else "✗",
             "–" if t["checks"] is None else ("pass" if t["checks"] == 1 else "fail"),
             "–" if t["judge"] is None else ("pass" if t["judge"] == 1 else "fail"))
            for i, t in enumerate(ts)]
    display(table(["Run", "Reward", "Code checks", "Judge"], rows))


show_case(REGRESSION_EXAMPLE)
t = BASELINE[REGRESSION_EXAMPLE][0]
display(Markdown(f"Final reply in run 1:\n\n{quote(t['reply'])}"
                 + (f"\n\nJudge critique:\n\n{quote(t['critique'])}" if t["critique"] else "")))
```

## 3. pass@k and pass^k {#metrics}

From `n` observed runs with `c` passes, `tests/eval/passk.py` estimates two different things about `k` future attempts:

- **pass@k**, the chance that **at least one** of `k` attempts passes: $1 - \binom{n-c}{k} / \binom{n}{k}$. It measures **capability**: can the agent do this at all if it gets several tries?
- **pass^k**, the chance that **all** `k` attempts pass: $\binom{c}{k} / \binom{n}{k}$. It measures **reliability**: will every user who asks get the right answer?

Both equal the pass rate $c/n$ at $k = 1$. As `k` grows, pass@k rises toward 1 and pass^k falls toward 0, unless the case always or never passes.

```{python}
case = CAPABILITY_EXAMPLE
res = json.loads((ROOT / f"eval_results/{case}-15.json").read_text())
n, c = res["n"], res["successes"]
ks = list(range(1, n + 1))
at = [pass_at_k(n, c, k) for k in ks]
hat = [pass_hat_k(n, c, k) for k in ks]

display(Markdown(
    f"Worked example, **{case}** after its {n} Part E runs ({c} passes): "
    f"pass@1 = pass^1 = {c / n:.2f}. With 3 attempts, the chance that at least one passes is "
    f"pass@3 = {pass_at_k(n, c, 3):.2f}, but the chance that all three pass is only pass^3 = {pass_hat_k(n, c, 3):.2f}. "
    f"At k = 5 the values are {pass_at_k(n, c, 5):.2f} and {pass_hat_k(n, c, 5):.2f}."
))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.4))
for ys, boot, color, label in [(at, pass_at_k_bootstrap, SERIES[0], "pass@k (at least one passes)"),
                               (hat, pass_hat_k_bootstrap, SERIES[1], "pass^k (all pass)")]:
    lo, hi = band(res["rewards"], ks, boot)
    ax.fill_between(ks, lo, hi, color=color, alpha=0.15, lw=0)
    ax.plot(ks, ys, color=color, lw=2, marker="o", ms=5, markeredgecolor=SURF, markeredgewidth=1.5)
    ax.annotate(label, (ks[6], ys[6]), xytext=(0, -16 if ys is at else 10), textcoords="offset points", color=INK, fontsize=9)
ax.set_xlabel("k (attempts)")
ax.set_ylabel("Estimated probability")
ax.set_ylim(-0.03, 1.05)
ax.set_xticks(ks)
ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID, lw=0.8)
ax.set_title(f"{case}: {c} of {n} runs passed", loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=11)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Shaded bands are 95% bootstrap percentile intervals: the observed runs are resampled with replacement 2,000 times and each estimate is recomputed. They show how much the estimate could move with a different draw of the same number of runs.

At baseline (`n = 5`), every case's metrics and the CI rule from `case_passes`:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-metrics
#| tbl-cap: "Baseline metrics (n = 5) and the CI decision each count would produce."
rows = []
for cid, ts in BASELINE.items():
    c = sum(t["reward"] == 1 for t in ts)
    kind = CASES[cid]["kind"]
    d = case_passes(kind, c, 5, CASES[cid].get("baseline_pass_rate"))
    rows.append((cid, kind, f"{c}/5", *(f"{pass_at_k(5, c, k):.2f}" for k in (1, 3, 5)),
                 *(f"{pass_hat_k(5, c, k):.2f}" for k in (3, 5)), str(d["decision"])))
display(table(["Case", "Kind", "Passes", "pass@1", "pass@3", "pass@5", "pass^3", "pass^5", "CI decision"], rows))
```

A regression case blocks CI on any failed run, which is the same as requiring pass^5 = 1 from five new runs. A capability case reports its numbers and never blocks. Even a reliable regression set fails sometimes: with `r` regression cases, each with per-run pass rate `p`, all `5r` runs pass with probability $p^{5r}$.

```{python}
r = kinds.count("regression")
display(table([f"Per-run pass rate p", f"P(all {5 * r} regression runs pass) = p^{5 * r}"],
              [(p, f"{p ** (5 * r):.3f}") for p in (0.95, 0.98, 0.99, 0.999)]))
```

## 4. GitHub Actions runs {#ci}

```{python}
display(Markdown(f"Pull request: <{CI['pull_request']}>. Agent model: `{CI['agent_model']}`. Case broken on purpose: **{CI['case_id']}**."))
rows = []
for label, run in [("1. Intentional regression", CI["regression_run"]), ("2. After the revert", CI["revert_run"])]:
    s = run["selected_case"]
    d = case_passes(s["kind"], s["observed_passes"], s["trials"])
    rows.append((label, f"`{run['commit']}`", run["change"], f"{s['observed_passes']}/{s['trials']}",
                 str(d["decision"]), run["result"], f"[run]({run['url']})"))
display(table(["Run", "Commit", "Change", f"{CI['case_id']} passes", f"{CI['case_id']} decision", "Job result", "Link"], rows))
other = CI["regression_run"].get("other_blocked_cases")
if other:
    display(Markdown(f"Run 1 also blocked on: {', '.join(other)}."))
display(Markdown(f"Explanation recorded in `ci-runs.json`:\n\n{quote(CI['explanation'])}"))
```

Each run's page shows the job summary table (pass count, pass@1, pass@3, pass@5, pass^5, and CI decision for every case) and has the `hw6-evals` Harbor job directory as a downloadable artifact.

## 5. Trial counts: 5, 10, and 15 observed runs {#trial-count}

Each case below ran 15 times on the same agent model as the baseline and CI runs. Each subset is the first `n` trials in Harbor's start order, as recorded in `eval_results/<case>-15.json`. **e-004** is the required Part E case (code checks only). **e-008** and **e-009** are capability cases decided by the frozen `narrates_or_overexplains-v6` judge.

```{python}
RESULTS = {cid: json.loads((ROOT / f"eval_results/{cid}-15.json").read_text()) for cid in TRIAL_COUNT_JOBS}
for cid, job in TRIAL_COUNT_JOBS.items():
    ts = trials(job, cid)
    assert [t["reward"] for t in ts] == RESULTS[cid]["rewards"], cid
    assert not any(t["error"] for t in ts), cid

rows = []
for cid, res in RESULTS.items():
    rows.append((cid, f"`{CASES[cid]['mode']}`", res["model"], f"{CASES[cid]['baseline_pass_rate']:.1f}",
                 marks(res["rewards"]), f"{res['successes']}/{res['n']}"))
display(table(["Case", "Mode", "Agent model", "Baseline rate", "15 runs in order", "Passes"], rows))
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-trial-count
#| tbl-cap: "pass@k at each observed run count, with the 95% bootstrap interval for pass@1."
for cid, res in RESULTS.items():
    rows = []
    for comp in res["comparisons"]:
        pak = comp["pass_at_k"]
        lo, hi = comp["pass_at_k_uncertainty"]["1"]["bootstrap_ci95"]
        rows.append((comp["n"], comp["successes"], f"{pak['1']:.2f} [{lo:.2f}, {hi:.2f}]",
                     *(f"{pak[k]:.2f}" if k in pak else "–" for k in ("3", "5", "10", "15")),
                     f"{comp['pass_hat_k']['5']:.2f}"))
    display(Markdown(f"**{cid}**"))
    display(table(["n", "Passes", "pass@1 [95% CI]", "pass@3", "pass@5", "pass@10", "pass@15", "pass^5"], rows))
```

```{python}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(RESULTS), 3, figsize=(7.5, 6.6), sharex=True, sharey=True)
for row, (cid, res) in zip(axes, RESULTS.items()):
    for ax, comp in zip(row, res["comparisons"]):
        n_, c_ = comp["n"], comp["successes"]
        ks = list(range(1, n_ + 1))
        lo, hi = band(res["rewards"][:n_], ks, pass_at_k_bootstrap)
        ax.fill_between(ks, lo, hi, color=SERIES[0], alpha=0.18, lw=0)
        ax.plot(ks, [pass_at_k(n_, c_, k) for k in ks], color=SERIES[0], lw=2, marker="o", ms=3.5,
                markeredgecolor=SURF, markeredgewidth=1)
        ax.set_title(f"{cid}, n = {n_} ({c_} passed)", loc="left", color=INK, fontsize=9)
        ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID, lw=0.8)
        ax.set_xlim(0.5, 15.5)
        ax.set_xticks([1, 5, 10, 15])
    row[0].set_ylabel("pass@k")
for ax in axes[-1]:
    ax.set_xlabel("k")
axes[0][0].set_ylim(-0.03, 1.05)
fig.suptitle("pass@k with 95% bootstrap intervals, from the first 5, 10, and 15 runs", x=0.01, ha="left", color=INK, fontsize=11)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Each column uses only the first `n` runs, so a curve stops at `k = n`. The band is the same 95% bootstrap interval as in the tables. When every observed run failed (e-009 at `n = 5`), every resample also fails, so the band collapses to zero width. That reflects the small sample, not certainty.

How much each estimate moved when runs were added:

```{python}
#| label: tbl-movement
#| tbl-cap: "Change in pass@k between observed run counts."
def delta(x):
    return f"{x:+.2f}" if round(x, 2) else "0.00"


rows = []
for cid, res in RESULTS.items():
    by_n = {comp["n"]: comp["pass_at_k"] for comp in res["comparisons"]}
    for k in ("1", "3", "5"):
        rows.append((cid, f"pass@{k}", *(f"{by_n[n][k]:.2f}" for n in (5, 10, 15)),
                     delta(by_n[10][k] - by_n[5][k]), delta(by_n[15][k] - by_n[10][k])))
display(table(["Case", "Metric", "n = 5", "n = 10", "n = 15", "Δ 5→10", "Δ 10→15"], rows))
```

### What the judge said in e-008 and e-009

In both judge-decided cases the code checks passed every run, so the judge decides each outcome.

```{python}
for cid in ("e-008", "e-009"):
    ts = trials(TRIAL_COUNT_JOBS[cid], cid)
    display(Markdown(
        f"**{cid}**: code checks passed {sum(t['checks'] == 1 for t in ts)}/{len(ts)}, "
        f"judge passed {sum(t['judge'] == 1 for t in ts)}/{len(ts)}."
    ))
    passing = [t for t in ts if t["judge"] == 1]
    failing = [t for t in ts if t["judge"] == 0]
    for t in passing + failing[:1]:
        verdict = "Judge pass" if t["judge"] == 1 else "Judge fail (example)"
        display(Markdown(f"*{verdict}, run {ts.index(t) + 1}.* Reply:\n\n{quote(t['reply'])}\n\nCritique:\n\n{quote(t['critique'])}"))
```
